title: Extend standalone paid-history bounds to central scalars and nonuniform words (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Extend the standalone finite ordinary-module paid-history argument of [#5425](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/tree/00005c8c5e81c7f27b5769f9309ff88758e26f51/research/fanout-optimality-support) in two scalar regimes. This is a [documentation-only proof contribution](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0d0bcf3fa261c9591e7e60ed5926c6e04d360f9e/docs/research/standalone-history-scalar-ceiling/README.md) with separate independent AI static reviews. It supplies no new paid-history principle, physical construction, admitted supplier or κ.

Both variants require ordinary initial history, distinct independent target input coordinates, invertible nonordinary target maps, fixed whole-field capacity and one actual new output row per paid call. Finite feedback and overwritten rows remain allowed.

| Extension | Exact domain |
| --- | --- |
| Central normalizers | One fixed finite columnwise word with exterior c·2^(n f), c in Q(i) and integer n fixed per instruction. Exactness holds at every positive width or throughout a consecutive infinite tail. |
| Eventual pointwise scalars | Arbitrary exterior c(f), nonuniform finite words and finite N(f), with one fixed finite ordinary one-column group G and geometry. The bound holds **at each f≥2p−1**, where p=\|PG\| counts actual projective classes. No practical or arbitrary small-width bound is claimed. |

In either domain, q qualifying target rows require at least q actual paid returns. The new note retains the self-contained proofs and distinguishes their width assumptions. Its q=120 example is a conditional LOCAL nomination of the ordered map T=A Jbar A^-1, with copied nonmonomial and full-current-input arguments. The physical BC ABI and implementation are not newly proved or admitted. The optional fixed P/T signed-profile consequence keeps the original optimistic target grants; it is not new funding.

Neither variant charges 120 additional calls at an actual parent cut containing paid/native/cached observations. Such correctly versioned observations can remove the additional charge. Shared conversions, changed ordinary groups or geometry, cross-column maps, changed capacities, several returns per call, dependent inputs, approximation and recursive compiler/precision/stock costs remain separate.

## Task and overlap

User-assigned ceiling and verification support; scope key `standalone-paid-history-scalar-extensions`. Scope is **changed** from #5425's fixed-scalar 112-output application to the two stated scalar/width contracts and a separate conditional source nomination. This is written mathematics with static review, rather than a proof-assistant formalization.

Base: `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`. Proof/review snapshot: `56c52a79f7663bc59ad3a5013c242a113039a701`. Publication head: `0d0bcf3fa261c9591e7e60ed5926c6e04d360f9e`; the second commit changes only HANDOFF.md to pin that snapshot; the third escapes Markdown table delimiters in README.md without changing mathematics.

The direct predecessor is #5425 at `00005c8c5e81c7f27b5769f9309ff88758e26f51`, including its feedback/overwrite history argument and ordinary-initial, fixed-capacity contract. The precise additions are central scalar normalizers, eventual pointwise arbitrary scalars/nonuniform finite words, and the separate conditional 120-coordinate application. Its 112-output source specialization is not transferred.

[#5436](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/4c31fd7d4eee61ff9fd59533549a67ef1a25b449) supplied the support-width prompt; its four-control 2705-source corollary is not adopted. Adjacent [#5441](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/11fedb46fa199283f78282187c10aea432d8b0bb) concerns fixed physical transfer-table endpoints and cut dimensions. [#5442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/commit/19e8f0452c09cbfe99511ea697fa239c1f457314) states a finite-group lifting lemma, but its separate complete-body claim is [challenged by review 6385984727](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5442#issuecomment-6385984727); that closure is not a dependency here. A small-width affine result for a different operator family cannot replace the large fixed ordinary-group/coset argument. A final refresh through 2026-10-24 17:10:39 UTC records an author repair of #5442 at `4d5abe038ac106bd79acf548df4aeb66f32eff09`; independent revalidation was not present. The challenged frozen head and subsequent repair are neither dependencies nor independently validated endpoint evidence for this note.

The supplied sole-monitor prepublication check covers 100 recent all-state PR-metadata/body records through 2026-10-24 16:50:42 UTC, with a later static locator addendum. Main/guidance/selected are unchanged. This bounded incremental check is not exhaustive novelty, Discussion or unpublished-work coverage.

## Validation

The sixteen-file note contains twelve unchanged proof/acceptance/review/source payloads and four new navigation/provenance documents. The sealed scalar-extension lemmas received independent AI static mathematical reviews without a required correction. Their original PROPOSED headings are preserved; additive reports and decisions record acceptance.

Copied-byte hashes and lengths, JSON/navigation, exact path scope, seven handoff labels and Git whitespace/diff checks are recorded as passive assembly checks. They are not theorem or supplier certificates. Separate independent static reviews cover the mathematical variants and polished documentation scope. Committed-byte and exact-path checks are separate custody evidence; hosted outcomes remain tied to the PR head.

There is no verifier, VERIFY manifest, numerical RESULT or scientific reproduction command. No operator, native/phase/rank/calibration, Powers/price, Lean or registered replay was run for the note. Source-native facts remain conditional inherited premises, not a new executable closure. The checkout is shallow/shared; no complete history or file corpus is claimed. The CI-navigation repair is already canonical and has no duplicate delta.

## Credit

Retain the #5425 ordinary-module proof and independent reviewer as the direct paid-history predecessor, and zxv's #5436 support-width prompt. Anthony Chefles supplies the classical multi-copy/projective tensor-independence precedent ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.64.062305)); the field-linear proof used here is stated directly. Peter Kropholler and Karl Lorensen's strong-rank theorem ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2019.08.014)) corroborates the self-contained central argument.

Credit the scalar/source authors, root's localization and paid-history question, independent reviewers, sole literature worker and BC/native/Clifford/product/compiler/precision/analytic lineage. Preserve Ali Romman, Dillon Amburgey/dillona, Cao Yifan, Cinna Davis, zxv, Dugongue, Jacob Alan Sussman, Chris R/Clear1nsight and the retained notices. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. AI static review is not independent human or formal-kernel verification.

## Open next questions

Identify the actual cut's available history module with source versions, owners, paid observations and lifetimes, then test containment of the required target rows and charge acquisition/retention once. That question is not decided by this standalone theorem. A smaller sufficient source-specific width guard needs a justified subgroup or span argument; no such cutoff is computed here. Recursive use also needs its own uniform cost, productive-target, precision and stock contract.
